Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment summary:
  - Clinical presentation: ~2 months of prominent anxiety temporally related to starting a new job with avoidance, anticipatory morning panic, irregular/racing palpitations lasting minutes (up to ~10 minutes), marked sleep disruption (~3–4 hours, shallow), daytime fatigue, reduced enjoyment of activities, social avoidance.
  - No prior similar episodes reported; no suicidal ideation.
  - Family history significant for maternal depression.
- Diagnostic reasoning (DDx integrated where consistent):
  - Most likely: Adjustment disorder with anxiety (work-related) — high likelihood given clear temporal relation to new job, symptoms focused on work situation, and functional impairment.
  - Possible: Generalized anxiety disorder — features overlap but duration (~2 months) is less than the 6-month threshold, so medium likelihood.
  - Cardiac cause: Paroxysmal arrhythmia (e.g., SVT/AF) — medium likelihood; palpitations described as irregular and lasting minutes, so cardiac rhythm disturbance cannot be excluded without ECG/monitoring.
  - Endocrine cause: Hyperthyroidism — low-to-moderate likelihood; can produce palpitations/anxiety — appropriate to exclude with blood tests.
  - Substance-related contributors (alcohol, nicotine) considered but less likely as primary driver; DDx notes possible contribution from binge alcohol or stimulant exposure.
- Contradictions/conflicts:
  - No substantive conflicts between transcript and DDx; DDx expands possible organic causes consistent with transcript findings.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Adjustment disorder with anxiety (work-related) — High likelihood
  - Justification: Onset ~2 months after starting a stressful new job; symptoms focused on work; marked functional impairment (sleep loss, social avoidance, reduced enjoyment).
- Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) — Moderate likelihood
  - Justification: Clinical features (excessive worry, insomnia, fatigue, reduced enjoyment) are consistent, but duration (~2 months) is below the 6-month criterion for GAD.
- Paroxysmal cardiac arrhythmia (e.g., SVT/AF) — Moderate likelihood
  - Justification: Patient describes irregular, fast palpitations lasting minutes to ~10 minutes at rest (in bed); cardiac rhythm disturbance cannot be excluded without ECG/ambulatory monitoring.
